report.source_text: MRI of the spine with gadolinium enhancement showed T2-weighted lesions in the dorsal region of the spinal cord. The spinal cord showed multiple regions of patchy hyperintensity, seen in the thoracic region of the spinal cord both centrally and peripherally (figure 1). The subarachnoid space was normal and the lumbosacral region was normal, ruling out cauda equina.

report.source_text: The lumbar puncture cerebral spinal fluid (CSF) analysis for aquaporin-4 antibodies, anti-myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein (anti-MOG) antibodies, protein, glucose, oligoclonal bands, microscopy, cultures and sensitivities, and viral PCR (including human T-cell leukaemia virus type 1 and SARS-CoV-2) all returned negative. CSF protein was 0.4 g, white cell count <0.001×109/L, red cell count 0.0002×1012/L with no organisms.

report.source_text: Throughout her admission, she was seen by the physiotherapy team and improved to mobilising short distances independently. She was discharged with a weaning regimen of prednisolone and co-trimoxazole 960 mg orally once daily for pneumocystis pneumonia prophylaxis until weaned past 30 mg prednisolone.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Acute longitudinal extensive transverse myelitis (LETM) secondary to COVID-19
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 35-year-old woman presented with sharp right-sided thoracic back pain at T8, progressive bilateral leg numbness, impaired walking, urinary retention, and constipation. She tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 by nasopharyngeal swab on admission. MRI spine with contrast showed patchy T2 hyperintense lesions in the thoracic spinal cord consistent with LETM; brain MRI was mostly unremarkable. CSF analysis was negative for aquaporin-4 and anti-MOG antibodies, viral PCR including SARS-CoV-2, with normal protein and cell counts, ruling out infectious and other autoimmune etiologies. She was treated with high-dose IV methylprednisolone followed by oral prednisolone and supportive care including catheterization and laxatives. During admission, she improved to mobilizing short distances independently and was discharged on a steroid weaning regimen with pneumocystis pneumonia prophylaxis.
